summary.title: DevOps - Wikipedia
summary.one_liner: DataOps is a set of practices that applies agile engineering, automation and statistical process control to data analytics pipelines to improve quality, speed and collaboration.
takeaways: DevOps merges software development and IT operations, guided by shared ownership, workflow automation and rapid feedback.
DORA metrics (deployment frequency, lead time, change failure rate, recovery time) measure delivery efficiency and reliability.
DataOps applies DevOps and agile ideas to the full data lifecycle, using SPC to monitor analytics pipelines.
DataOps originated around 2014 and was popularized by Andy Palmer and Steph Locke; Gartner placed it on the 2018 Hype Cycle.
The page also covers related areas: GitOps, database DevOps, mobile DevOps, DevSecOps and SRE.
summary.summary: This Wikipedia article covers DevOps broadly, including its history, DORA metrics, and related approaches such as Agile, CI/CD, GitOps, DevSecOps, and SRE. The section most relevant to the DataOps listing is a subsection that defines DataOps as practices combining process-oriented data perspectives, automation, and agile engineering methods to improve data analytics. It explains the use of statistical process control for monitoring pipelines, its history from a 2014 blog post, and its goals of velocity, reliability, and quality. The article is a reference-style overview with many citations rather than a hands-on guide.
